newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Prodi goes to presidential palace.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Prodi goes to presidential palace.

text.p: Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi was holding talks with President Oscar Luigi Scalfaro on Wednesday after his hard-left ally in parliament opposed him in a vote to send an Italian-led security force to Albania.
Deployment of the force was overwhelmingly approved by the lower house of parliament but without the support of Communist Refoundation, which normally secures Prodi's majority.
Political sources said Scalfaro was expected to send Prodi back to parliament for a confidence vote in the coming days to decide whether his 11-month-old government could survive.

Prodi, facing the stiffest political challenge in 11 months in office, staved off an immediate government crisis when the centre-right opposition Freedom Alliance said it would vote with his centre-left coalition on a joint motion.

The motion passed by 503 votes to 85 but the opposition exacted a high price for siding with the government, forcing Prodi into a humiliating admission in parliament that he was not able to muster a majority of his own on the policy.

"I declare now that if the dissent expressed by the Communist Refoundation group persists, I will go immediately to the head of state to inform him officially of the situation and await his evalution," Prodi said at the start of the debate.
